(a) The trigger node is a nameless BLOCK under a BLOCK recording "foo" with no SCRIPT. Hops 1-4 are faithful to their docs (null guard; own record; pass-throughs for a node with no record of its own); their wrong result is inherited. The gold is the only method that consults ancestors and decides where the walk stops; its contract ('the name of the source file that a node belongs to'), read in the chain's own vocabulary (hop 2: a node that records a name belongs to that file; facade: the source name property on the node or its ancestors), is violated when it walks past the recording parent and returns null. (b) No hop javadoc contradicts its code; hops 3-4 state a precondition that hop 2 guarantees, and none promises to consult ancestors. (c) No competing repair: every passing non-gold edit either re-implements the ancestor walk in a hop so that hops 3-4 and the gold are never reached on the trigger (their output is constant null for the parentless nameless nodes they still see) -- bypasses -- or is a partial parent-only patch that still violates the facade contract for a grandparent-recorded node. Re-pointing the gold's start (declared hop-3 compensator) fails, since the gold stops only at a SCRIPT and the trigger tree has none. (d) Names are neutral host vocabulary; the variant gold reads as an ordinary find-enclosing-SCRIPT loop; the facade lie (a node-keyed map cache) names neither the fault nor the omitted stop rule; the misindented javadoc opener is shared with hop 2 (both end-of-class insertions), so it does not single out the gold. (e) Gold is exactly five calls below the facade; hops in five distinct existing classes (Parser, JSTypeRegistry, Compiler.CodeBuilder, TokenStream, TypeCheck); facade body is one delegating call (original had no guard); one added procedural sentence; gold javadoc silent on the stop rule; existing trigger, empty test.patch, sole new failure. (f) The convention that a non-SCRIPT node's record names the file of what lies below it is pinned outside the gold: the facade's @return text, NodeTraversal.traverseAtScope and SyntacticScopeCreator.scanRoot (and, unlisted, TypedScopeCreator's shouldTraverse) take a function scope's file from the FUNCTION node's own record, and Node.copyInformationFrom / IRFactory templated node creation put records on ordinary nodes.
notes: Recorded bypasses (all pass trigger, ownership tests and full suite): hop-2 self-recursion on the parent, hop-3 re-entry into hop 2 at the parent, hop-1 self-recursion on the parent; each makes hops 3-4 and the gold unreachable on the trigger.
